newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ports of Auckland extension could start mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Ports of Auckland extension could start mid-1997.

text.p: Ports of Auckland Ltd on Tuesday welcomed the decision to approve its second option for the extension of Fergusson Container Terminal.
If no appeals were lodged, detailed design work would now begin and construction could start in mid-1997, Ports of Auckland said.
The approval was announced by the joint Auckland Regional Council and Auckland City Council Commission which considered the resource consent application for the project.
Chief Executive Geoff Vazey said the option that was approved was a compromise which should address the concerns of yachting and boating enthusiasts.
Stringent conditions had also been imposed on noise.
"It still allows us to provide the additional facilities which we need to meed the growing demands of importers and exporters in the Auckland region," Vazey said.

The Commissioners also required a public walkway to be provided along the eastern side of the reclamation, outside the terminal area. At this stage the decision was considered to be a workable one, Ports of Auckland said.
